thread:
IncidentBot: ALERT: Service 'api-generation' is seeing elevated 500s in us-west-2 (error rate 18% > 10% threshold). Paging oncall @Maya R.
Maya R: on it, picking up the page. seeing spikes in tail latency too. starting triage.
Maya R: quick check — are we seeing any autoscale activity or instance churn? `aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:service,Values=api-generation`
Jon T: I saw autoscale flapping earlier, but that was resolved at 14:22. current ASG stable. logs show a lot of upstream timeout errors to s3://model-cache in the last 3 mins.
Liam K: copying vendor contact info from runbook and opening support case with cloud provider. Case note: "High 500s from internal model cache reads in us-west-2; possible S3 control-plane throttling or EFS latency." Escalating to priority P1.
Maya R: thanks. Sara — can you start drafting a customer-facing status snippet? We need one for the status page and a short email for active customers.
Sara P: on it. Drafting: `We are currently investigating elevated errors impacting text generation requests in us-west-2. Our on-call is engaged and we are working with our cloud provider to mitigate. Users may experience increased errors or latency for a subset of requests. No data loss is expected.` Want me to mention ETA?
Maya R: put ETA TBD; we'll update in 15m. Also add guidance: `If you need immediate assistance, please contact support with incident ID INC-1751002345.`
Jon T: update from cloud support via phone: they see increased 5xx from S3 control plane in us-west-2 tied to a micro-region control-plane redeploy. They opened an internal ticket, engineers are rolling a fix. ETA 30-45m per their estimate. Support case # 3512345678.
Maya R: noted. Starting a safe fallback: rolling config to prefer cached model on local instance and reduce S3 read fanout. Liam please coordinate the rollout.
Liam K: patch ready, testing canary on 2 instances in us-west-2 now. command:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/api-worker CACHE_FALLBACK=local --record
kubectl rollout status deploy/api-worker -n inference
```
Maya R: good. after canary, if stable, roll across the ASG. Monitor error rates and token success % in Console.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status changed -> investigating (Cloud provider escalated).
Jon T: cloud support sent an update: mitigation in progress, they are draining control-plane nodes; they expect transient errors to continue for a while. Also provided a support link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/3512345678
Sara P: status page draft for publising (copy to be posted):
```
Summary: Elevated errors affecting Redwood API generation endpoints in us-west-2.
Impact: Some customers may see increased 5xx errors or timeouts for text generation requests.
Current status: We are actively investigating and mitigating with our cloud provider. A temporary fallback is being rolled out to reduce dependence on remote model cache.
Next update: in 15 minutes or as we have new information.
```
Maya R: small ask — add a bullet for "Workaround for affected apps: reduce parallelism or retry with exponential backoff to lower error surface."
Sara P: added. prepping to post to status.redwood.ai once we confirm the canary is stable.
Liam K: canary passed on 2/2 instances, error rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% in canary slice. Kicking full rollout now.
IncidentBot: ALERT: oncall handoff scheduled in 35 minutes to next oncall Jon T.
Maya R: rolling out completed — monitoring. thanks team.
Jon T: received handoff ack. I'll keep the vendor case open and push for final root cause and timeline for full control-plane stabilization.
Maya R: customer notification email (short):
```
Subject: Incident: Elevated errors for generation endpoints in us-west-2 (INC-1751002345)
Body: We are investigating an incident causing increased errors for text generation in us-west-2. Our team has implemented a temporary fallback to reduce customer impact and is working with our cloud provider on a fix. We will update you within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption.
```
Sara P: sending to support@redwood.ai for triage to affected customers now.
Jon T: cloud support just updated: control-plane redeploy completed, but they are monitoring residual 5xx spikes as caches rehydrate. Recommend keeping fallback in place for 1 hour then reassess.
Maya R: sounds good. Leave fallback for 60 minutes. I'll close the thread after postmortem action items are drafted.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation deployed; monitoring.
Sara P: posted status page and sent customer emails. Slack thread for customers: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-1751002345 (placeholder).
Liam K: saving logs and metrics snapshot to S3: `s3://redwood-incident-archives/1751002345/`
Maya R: great work everyone. Postmortem owners: Liam (technical RCA) and Sara (customer comms). Jon will follow up with cloud provider to gather timeline. We'll aim to have a 72h postmortem drafted.
Jon T: ack. I'll request full control-plane event logs from cloud support case.
Maya R: closing active coordination — if anything new appears, ping @oncall. :thumbsup:
